reference.title: TIP: Token Importance in On-Policy Distillation
reference.authors: Yuanda Xu, Hejian Sang, Zhengze Zhou, Ran He, Zhipeng Wang, Alborz Geramifard
reference.notes_page: https://aipapernotes.alphaavatar.io/llm/training/RL/OPD/2026/TIP (provided by the maintainer; not read for this record)
reference.read_for_this_record: the arXiv abstract page only (2026-10-21 UTC); the full text has not been read

what_the_abstract_states: a two-axis taxonomy of token positions by student entropy and teacher-student divergence, for on-policy distillation where the student trains on its own rollouts under token-level teacher supervision
selected regions: high student entropy, and low student entropy with high teacher-student divergence (overconfident wrong predictions)

reported: keeping 50% of tokens by entropy-based sampling matches or exceeds all-token training while cutting peak memory by up to 47%; under 10% of tokens from the low-entropy/high-divergence region nearly matches full-token baselines
the abstract does not state the KL direction or the prefix construction
maintainer_notes: the original method uses student-generated prefixes and KL(student || teacher) -- to be confirmed from the full text before any design is frozen
a selection that keeps only high-entropy positions misses low-entropy/high-divergence positions; the combination is the point
teacher-student divergence is not an independent gold: it says where the student disagrees, not that the teacher is right
candidates.hypothesis: concentrating distillation on positions selected by student entropy combined with teacher-student divergence transfers more reasoning per supervised position than all-token distillation, at matched trajectories and matched KL
applicability: the faithful method is ON-POLICY: it needs student rollouts, a rollout service and the Stage-4/5 ownership, cost and authorization that come with them
an offline, teacher-forced, forward-KL variant would be a TIP-INSPIRED ADAPTATION and is never called a reproduction

future_comparison_design.controls: trajectory distribution, KL direction and token-selection rule varied ONE at a time
future_comparison_design.baseline: an all-token arm with the SAME trajectory protocol and the SAME KL (direction and temperature), so the selection rule is the only difference
future_comparison_design.endpoint: eval-set-1 formal fluid correctness and the per-axis and supporting reports, as in H1; memory and throughput reported separately
not_now: the paper's reported gains are not this project's
